claims.text: The component material is predisposed to hot cracking when exposed to fusion-welding temperatures.
Friction stir repair is a solid-state process that locally reworks material without melting it.
Friction stir repair will produce a refined microstructure in the damaged zone.
Friction stir repair will produce a recrystallized microstructure in the damaged zone.
Intense plastic deformation during friction stir repair causes microstructural refinement and recrystallization.
The refined, recrystallized microstructure minimizes residual stresses.
The refined, recrystallized microstructure minimizes the formation of brittle phases.
Friction stir repair avoids the thermal gradients and liquid-phase solidification associated with fusion-weld repair.
Avoiding melting, severe thermal gradients, and liquid-phase solidification mitigates hot cracking.
Friction-stir-repaired components will have a lower incidence of hot cracking than fusion-weld-repaired components.
Friction-stir-repaired components will have higher tensile performance than fusion-weld-repaired components.
Friction-stir-repaired components will have better fatigue performance than fusion-weld-repaired components.
Traditional fusion-weld repairs suffer from hot cracking under the stated aggressive conditions.
Traditional fusion-weld repairs exhibit degraded mechanical performance under the stated aggressive conditions.
Elevated sub-melting-point temperatures and cyclic mechanical loads represent the component's aggressive service environment.
Repair quality will vary with friction stir process parameters and material-specific responses.
